content:
sam: heads up — on runner-03 I see gradual memory growth when serving many 8k+ contexts. Started after last compaction change. flame graph: https://internal/fg/176754 — looks like hot path in kv fragment iterator and page attach.
asha: can you paste a couple of log lines from the canary?
sam: sure, snip from /var/log/runner-03/kvcache.log:
```
[2026-05-12 09:12:34] [kv_cache] evict fragment idx=4288 off=32 len=64 owner=req-41
[2026-05-12 09:12:34] [kv_cache] attach fragment idx=4288 off=16 len=64 owner=req-39
[2026-05-12 09:12:34] [kv_cache] read fragment idx=4288 off=16 tag=0x7f owner=req-39
```
sam: note the same idx with different offset and owners — smells like stale fragment metadata being reused.
miguel: that pattern usually means we reused a fragment slot without zeroing the tag/offset. Could be a race between compaction and attach. Did you see any concurrent compaction logs?
sam: yes, compactor started right before the growth: `compactor: split fragment idx=4288 -> [4288, 4296]` then shortly after those attach/read lines.
nina: hypothesis: when we split a fragment during compaction we update the physical pages but fail to rewrite the logical token offset for the new fragment header. Later request attaches to the slot and reads with stale offset => wrong token alignment (cross-request contamination).
asha: can you grep for request ids referencing that idx?
sam: quick grep output:
```
req-39: attach idx=4288 off=16 ctx_len=8200
req-41: evict idx=4288 off=32 ctx_len=1024
req-48: attach idx=4288 off=16 ctx_len=4096
```
sam: different requests, different contexts, same fragment index.
miguel: ok that confirms cross-request references. Two short fixes: 1) ensure compaction path clears fragment header tag/offset before reuse, 2) add an assert in page_attach to reject mismatched owner/tag.
perf-bot: profiling note — adding the assert increases p50 token latency by ~0.3ms on microbench. Acceptable for canary.
miguel: I'll prototype a small patch on branch `fragments/index-sanitize` — add header zeroing + unit test that simulates split+attach race.
sam: opened PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/fragments/pull/234 — includes repro harness and flaky test.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started: runner-03 -> 10% traffic (fragments/index-sanitize)
nina: we should also add a long-context integration test that runs multi-turn interleaved requests for 10 minutes to catch leaks. Also check Private on-disk metadata migrations — old images might not zero headers.
asha: agree. next steps: miguel will land the assert+sanitize, sam will add the long-run repro to perf harness, nina will draft migration note for Private.
sam: thanks — I'll keep monitoring memory and post updated flamegraphs. :thumbsup:
